Our Korean legal team approved the Korean refund policy below in October 2026, and it is the current version. The English is an older draft that has not been updated. Keep the approved Korean as it is unless there is an actual language error, and tell me where the English no longer matches.

Korean (approved, current):
구독을 해지하면 남은 기간의 요금을 일할 계산해 환불합니다. 단, 연간 요금제를 결제일로부터 7일이 지난 후 해지하면 환불 금액의 10%를 위약금으로 공제합니다.

English (older): Cancellations receive a prorated refund for the remaining period. Annual plans canceled after 14 days are not eligible for a refund.
output:
구독을 해지하면 남은 기간의 요금을 일할 계산해 환불합니다. 단, 연간 요금제를 결제일로부터 7일이 지난 후 해지하면 환불 금액의 10%를 위약금으로 공제합니다.

I left the approved Korean unchanged because it has no language errors. The older English differs in two places:
- Cutoff: English says annual plans canceled after 14 days; the Korean says after 7 days from the payment date.
- Consequence: English says no refund at all after that point; the Korean still refunds, but deducts a 10% cancellation fee from the refund amount.
The English should be updated to match the Korean.

English: Pro plan: US$24 per user/month, billed annually. Prices exclude VAT. You can cancel at any time. Annual plans are not refundable for the unused part of the term.

Korean: 프로 요금제: 사용자당 월 29,000원(부가세 포함), 연간 결제. 연간 결제 후 7일 이내에 해지하면 전액 환불해 드립니다.

[부가세 표기 확정 필요]
[해지 및 환불 조건 확정 필요]

This isn't a final block yet, because the two versions disagree on commercial terms and I can't tell which one governs:
- Price: US$24 per user/month, VAT excluded (English) vs. 29,000원 per user/month, VAT included (Korean).
- Cancellation/refund: English says you can cancel at any time and annual plans aren't refundable for the unused term; Korean says full refund if canceled within 7 days of annual payment (and doesn't mention cancel-anytime).
Only the plan name, per-user monthly pricing, and annual billing are common to both.

One question: which version is current and approved, the English from the global team or the Korean from the Korea team? Once you tell me, I'll fill in the three bracketed lines and give you the final Korean block.

input:
I'm replying to a customer who emailed about a damaged item. A teammate wrote the English reply and then translated it into Korean. Please check the Korean before I send it.

English: Thank you for contacting us about your order. Could you send us the receipt so we can review whether the order is eligible for a refund? We'll get back to you once we've reviewed it.

Korean: 주문 관련 문의해 주셔서 감사합니다. 영수증을 보내 주시면 전액 환불해 드리겠습니다. 확인이 끝나면 다시 안내드리겠습니다.
output:
주문 관련 문의해 주셔서 감사합니다. 환불 가능 여부를 검토할 수 있도록 영수증을 보내 주실 수 있을까요? 확인이 끝나면 다시 안내드리겠습니다.

Note: The Korean draft promised a full refund once you receive the receipt ("전액 환불해 드리겠습니다"). The English only asks for the receipt so you can review eligibility, so I changed it to match.
